answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-refundable stake before it may place bids, with larger limits unlocked only after counterparties confirm completed work. A sybil attacker can mint keys cheaply, but each one must tie up real capital and risk losing it when a job is abandoned or disputed. At the nadir of trust, a harbor of verified counterparties can keep trading cautiously until dawn, while fresh identities remain costly and low-limit.
